**Bring your engineering expertise to processes that help protect lives every day

**Do you enjoy solving complex manufacturing challenges and turning technical insight into lasting improvements?

At Bavarian Nordic, we are looking for a Engineering Specialist to strengthen our Drug Substance manufacturing processes and support the introduction of new equipment and technologies.

You will join Material & Sterile Operation, reporting to the Senior Manager, and combine hands-on problem-solving with technical leadership. Your work will help ensure that our processes deliver reliable performance, consistent quality, and GMP compliance.

**Your impact

**As a technical expert for your assigned process areas, you will help develop, optimize, validate, and maintain manufacturing processes throughout their lifecycle. You will challenge existing solutions, identify risks before they affect production, and turn improvement opportunities into practical results.

Working across Manufacturing, Engineering, Automation, and Quality, you will also share your expertise and strengthen process understanding across teams.

**What You Will Do

**

• Improve process performance: Lead process design and optimization, address bottlenecks and operational risks, and troubleshoot complex manufacturing challenges to improve efficiency, reliability, and quality.

• Provide expertise in CIP/SIP: Act as a Subject Matter Expert for Cleaning-in-Place and Sterilization-in-Place systems, improving system design, component selection, and cleaning and sterilization strategies.

• Introduce equipment and technologies: Guide technical activities from specifications and vendor design reviews through factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, qualification, and validation.

• Support validation and technology transfer: Develop validation strategies, lead and support Process Performance Qualification (PPQ), and drive the transfer of processes into manufacturing or between sites.

• Strengthen compliance: Lead and support deviations, root cause investigations, CAPAs, change controls, and risk assessments. Represent your technical areas during audits and inspections.

• Develop technical capability: Coach colleagues, provide training, and share engineering knowledge to strengthen process understanding and consistent execution.

**What You Bring

**You hold a master’s degree in Chemical, Bioprocess, Process, or Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline, and have at least 10 years of industrial process engineering experience.

You bring:

• A strong track record in process design, optimization, and structured troubleshooting within GMP manufacturing. Experience in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, vaccines, or another highly regulated industry is strongly preferred.

• Extensive hands-on expertise in CIP/SIP design, operation, and optimization.

• In-depth knowledge of process equipment, piping, valves, and instrumentation, together with an understanding of how process and automation systems interact.

• Experience with equipment introduction, qualification, validation, PPQ, and technology transfer, including changes requiring regulatory approval.

• Solid knowledge of pharmaceutical quality systems and regulatory expectations, with practical experience in investigations, CAPAs, change controls, risk assessments, and inspection support.

**How You Work

**You combine analytical thinking with practical judgement and take ownership of moving issues towards resolution.

You are comfortable questioning established practices and can explain why a proposed change will improve process performance or reduce risk.

You communicate complex technical topics clearly, build constructive relationships across functions, and balance attention to detail with an understanding of production needs and business priorities. You also enjoy helping others develop through coaching, knowledge sharing, and collaboration.

**An opportunity to grow your leadership

**This role offers the opportunity to make an immediate impact through technical leadership. For the right candidate, it may also provide a pathway into formal people management, potentially leading a team of approximately 8–10 Process Engineers.

Progression will depend on demonstrated performance, sound judgement, and the ability to develop others, build an inclusive team environment, and translate business priorities into practical execution.

**Why join Bavarian Nordic?

**At Bavarian Nordic, we work to protect lives through vaccines. Your engineering expertise will contribute directly to the manufacturing processes that make this possible.

You will have opportunities to influence technical solutions, support important technology transfers, and see your improvements become part of daily operations. Guided by our values—Persisting Pioneers, Embracing Change, and Boosted by the Team—we work together to solve challenges and strengthen our capabilities

**Ready to make a difference? Apply now!

**Apply by clicking the ‘APPLY’ button. We are interviewing on an ongoing basis and look forward to receiving your CV.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

**For us, it is all about improving and saving lives

**Improving and saving lives through innovative vaccines is at the heart of what we do at Bavarian Nordic. We are a fully integrated vaccine company focused on the development, manufacturing and commercialisation of life-saving vaccines, and the largest pure-play vaccine company in the world.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

__Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

_For more information, visit _**www.bavarian-nordic.com

jobs.occupation: Maximizing use of fresh grass for dairy cows by combining grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Animal and Veterinary Sciences programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Research area and project description:

We are seeking a dedicated PhD student for a 3-year position within the topic of dairy production with fresh grass as a main forage source.

The impact of dairy production on environment and climate is of continued importance and interest. Cropping and feeding fresh grass can potentially improve the impact of dairy production on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen leakage to surrounding fresh waters.

The project investigates the potential of maximizing fresh grass forage intake to reduce enteric methane emission and increase nitrogen utilization, while maintaining milk production. A series of trials with lactating dairy cows are planned investigating combinations of grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards.

This project offers:

• A unique opportunity to contribute to a more sustainable agriculture and environmental-friendly milk production

• An active and stimulating academic environment with several other PhD students and early career staff

• Access to state-of-the-art research facilities for both barn-housing, grazing, and pasture management for dairy cattle

• Collaboration with a range of research partners

• Collaborative projects that foster innovative thinking and practical implementation

Qualifications and specific competences:

Applicants to the PhD position must hold a relevant university degree (MSc) in Animal Science, Agricultural Science, or related fields.

The candidate is expected to have:

• Understanding of ruminant nutrition and digestion

• Experience with data handling and analysis using at least one software.

• Ability and interest in collaborating across disciplines with project partners.

• Ability to communicate effectively in English.

• Good scientific and writing skills.

Place of employment and place of work:

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, Research center Foulum, Blichers allé 20, 8830 Tjele, Denmark.

Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:

jobs.occupation: Senior Simulation Engineer - Finite Element Analysis
jobs.description:
Senior Simulation Engineer – Finite Element Analysis

Hillerød, Denmark

Are you interested in using simulation to develop medical devices that help deliver treatments to patients worldwide? We are looking for an experienced Senior Simulation Engineer specializing in finite element analysis (FEA) to join our team in Hillerød and support the development and maintenance of drug delivery solutions.

Your new role

As our Senior Simulation Engineer, you will take technical ownership of structural simulation activities, helping teams develop reliable products and make informed design decisions. You will work across the product lifecycle, from evaluating early design concepts to supporting validation, product improvements and failure investigations.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Lead finite element analyses: Independently plan and execute structural simulations, selecting appropriate methods to assess performance, durability and safety under realistic loading conditions.

• Build reliable simulation models: Translate engineering requirements and CAD designs into robust models, defining geometry, meshes, material behavior, contacts and boundary conditions. Verify model quality through convergence and sensitivity studies.

• Support design optimization: Collaborate with design and mechanical engineers to improve product performance, material selection and cost. Provide practical recommendations and technical input during design reviews.

• Validate simulations against physical tests: Work with physical test and define validation activities, correlate simulation results with experimental data, assess uncertainty and refine models based on findings.

• Support product development and failure investigations: Contribute structural analysis expertise to cross-functional teams working on new products, product maintenance, validation and root cause analysis.

• Communicate findings clearly: Prepare reports and presentations that explain analysis methods, assumptions, results and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Advance simulation practices and develop colleagues: Improve simulation methods, workflows and standards, contribute to the structural simulation strategy, and mentor junior engineers and interns.

Your new department

You will join Drug Delivery Innovation (DDI), a new area within Novo Nordisk’s global organization, based in Hillerød.

Our team comprises 14 colleagues across three specialist groups: Structural Simulation, Molding Simulation and Material Science. We work closely together and collaborate with stakeholders across Novo Nordisk, combining expertise in simulation and materials to support the development and maintenance of drug delivery solutions.

In this role, you will contribute structural simulation expertise to projects involving design evaluation, test correlation and product improvements. Your findings will help teams assess design options and make decisions throughout development.

Your skills and qualifications

You bring a strong technical foundation and can independently lead complex simulation work, from defining the analysis approach to communicating recommendations that inform design decisions.

To succeed in this role, you have:

• A master’s degree in mechanical engineering, structural engineering, applied mechanics or a related discipline.

• Substantial practical FEA experience, including independent responsibility for complex structural analyses and recommendations.

• The ability to explain technical findings clearly and collaborate effectively with colleagues across design, testing, manufacturing and quality.

• A solid understanding of structural mechanics, material behavior, nonlinear analysis, contact modelling, fatigue and failure mechanisms.

• Experience validating simulation models against experimental data, assessing uncertainty and translating findings into practical design improvements.

Desirable experience

• Modelling of plastics, elastomers, paper and cardboard, including their material behavior and structural response.

• Working in a regulated industry, particularly pharmaceuticals or medical device development.

You take initiative, work systematically and communicate openly with colleagues and stakeholders. You can manage competing priorities as projects evolve and connect detailed technical findings to their implications for product performance and development decisions.

Working at Novo Nordisk

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

What we offer

Project Manager – Operations

Location: Lyngby, Denmark

Do you have a proven track record of turning complex operational challenges into tangible results? Are you motivated by getting close to manufacturing operations, analysing performance and working with teams to implement improvements that make a measurable difference?

We are looking for a Project Manager who combines strong analytical and problem-solving capability with the drive, resilience and hands-on approach required to deliver outcomes in complex manufacturing environments.

If you enjoy taking ownership, solving difficult problems and seeing your work translate into improved operational performance, this could be your next career move.

The position

As a Project Manager, you will work as part of our internal operations and manufacturing consulting team, delivering complex improvement, operational readiness and ramp up projects across our global manufacturing network.

This is not a traditional PMO or project coordination role.

You will be expected to get close to the operation, spend time on the shop floor, understand what is really happening within the production environment and use data and structured problem-solving to identify opportunities for improvement.

More importantly, your responsibility does not end when the solution has been identified. You will work alongside manufacturing teams and stakeholders to turn recommendations into actions and deliver tangible operational outcomes.

Our projects are typically intensive assignments, with project teams substantially dedicated to one project at a time. Assignments will often run for six to twelve months and can sometimes continue for longer.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Taking ownership of project workstreams and operational improvement initiatives from diagnosis through to implementation and delivery.

• Driving operational readiness and ramp-up of new production lines, helping manufacturing operations achieve stable target performance.

• Working directly with manufacturing sites and shop-floor teams to understand operational challenges and identify bottlenecks, losses and improvement opportunities.

• Analysing operational performance data and developing capacity models, process maps and improvement scenarios.

• Translating complex analysis into clear recommendations, practical implementation roadmaps and measurable actions.

• Driving implementation and following improvements through to tangible operational outcomes.

• Working with production teams to establish sustainable changes in performance and ways of working.

• Collaborating with stakeholders across manufacturing, engineering, quality, supply chain and site leadership.

• Influencing stakeholders and maintaining momentum when implementation is challenging or priorities change.

• Communicating progress, risks, recommendations and outcomes clearly to relevant stakeholders and project leadership.

This is a hands on role. You should be comfortable moving between analytical problem-solving and the realities of implementation on the manufacturing shop floor.

The position is based in Lyngby, Denmark, and requires flexibility for up to 50% global travel.

Travel requirements will depend on project assignment and may change throughout a project. The ability and willingness to travel flexibly according to business and project requirements is therefore an essential requirement of the position.

Qualifications

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate a proven track record of delivering outcomes, rather than simply participating in projects.

You combine strong intellectual and analytical capability with the practical judgement, resilience and persistence required to turn ideas into results.

To succeed in this role, you:

• Hold a relevant degree in engineering, science, business administration, economics or another relevant discipline.

• Have relevant professional experience within areas such as manufacturing, operational excellence, operations consulting, engineering, supply chain, procurement or complex cross-functional project work.

• Can demonstrate a proven track record of taking ownership and delivering tangible outcomes through projects, operational improvements or complex cross-functional initiatives.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and structured problem-solving capability.

• Are comfortable personally analysing operational data and using it to identify performance gaps, bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.

• Can translate analysis into practical recommendations and then follow those recommendations through implementation.

• Are comfortable working hands-on with manufacturing sites and shop-floor teams.

• Can operate effectively in complex and ambiguous environments where the solution may not initially be obvious.

• Demonstrate strong stakeholder management, collaboration and communication skills.

• Have the resilience and persistence to continue driving change when implementation is difficult or initial solutions do not deliver the expected results.

• Are professionally proficient in English.

• Are able and willing to travel globally for up to 50% of your time according to project requirements.

Relevant experience from operations or management consulting can be particularly valuable, including experience gained within operational practices or projects.

We are also interested in candidates from complex manufacturing environments such as pharmaceuticals, automotive, aerospace and FMCG, particularly where you have worked with operational improvement, production ramp-up, manufacturing performance or Lean ways of working.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing, GMP and validation experience are advantageous but are not essential.

Experience working within a Lean manufacturing environment can also be beneficial. Formal Lean certification is not required.

Likewise, formal project management qualifications such as PMP or PRINCE2 are not a requirement. We place greater emphasis on your demonstrated ability to structure problems, work with people, take ownership and deliver measurable outcomes.

About the department

You will join Drug Product Manufacturing Excellence, a global unit responsible for driving performance improvements, operational readiness and transformation across Novo's manufacturing network.

The team operates as an internal operations and manufacturing consultancy, supporting our manufacturing organisation with complex operational challenges.

Our colleagues bring diverse professional backgrounds, including operations and management consulting, Novo manufacturing and support functions, and industries such as automotive, aerospace and FMCG.

What brings the team together is the ability to combine analytical problem-solving with hands-on implementation.

Our projects can include operational readiness and ramp-up of new production lines, improving capacity and performance within existing operations and solving complex cross-functional manufacturing challenges.

Rather than managing several projects simultaneously, our project teams are typically substantially dedicated to one assignment, allowing them to work closely with the operation and remain involved from diagnosis through to implementation.

As a Project Manager, you will have meaningful ownership within these assignments and will be expected to demonstrate that your work ultimately translates into operational outcomes.

The role provides significant exposure to different manufacturing environments, functions and senior stakeholders across our global organisation and offers opportunities to progress towards increasingly complex project and leadership responsibilities.

Working at Novo

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordinary results we produce. Being part of a global healthcare company means opportunities to learn and develop are all around us, while our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind.
